title: THE GOD WHO BROUGHT YOU OUT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land
of Canaan and to be your God'" - Lev 25:38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God grounds all these commands about generosity in a single fact: I am the
LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt. Their kindness to the poor was
to flow from remembering their own rescue.

Think about the logic. You were slaves. You had nothing. I brought you out,
gave you a land, and became your God. Now, when your neighbour is where you
once were, remember what I did for you — and do likewise.

Dear reader, this is the engine of all Christian generosity. We do not give
in order to earn God's favour; we give because we have already received it.
Grace received becomes grace extended.

Jesus told of a servant forgiven an enormous debt who then refused to
forgive a small one, and He warned against that hardness of heart (Matt
18:32-33). John puts it simply: we love because He first loved us (1 John
4:19). Paul urges us to be kind and compassionate, forgiving each other,
just as in Christ God forgave us (Eph 4:32).

Every act of mercy we show is meant to be an echo of the mercy shown to us.
When generosity feels costly, the cure is to remember our own rescue. We too
were brought out of Egypt — out of slavery to sin, by the blood of Christ.

Let the memory of grace make you gracious today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the memory of God's mercy to me shape how I treat others?
2. Where have I received grace but been slow to extend it?
3. How can remembering my own rescue make me more generous?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You rescued me when I had nothing to offer. Let the memory of Your
grace flow out of me as mercy toward others today. Amen.
